newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies Clark quick end to refinery hearing.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies Clark quick end to refinery hearing.

text.p: The Illinois circuit court judge presiding over a hearing to determine whether or not a Clark Refining and Marketing plant at Blue Island, Ill. should be shut on safety grounds denied the company's motion for a summary dismissal.

Circuit court judge Albert Green said Thursday: "At this juncture, enough concern has been raised and there is evidence that has to be answered. This court wants to hear from Clark as to the safety of the facility in Blue Island."
Clark's 80,515 barrel-per-day (bpd) Blue Island plant had a fire on Saturday at a 1,000 bpd propane "scrubber" unit, which also shut a 6,400 bpd alkylation unit which helps produce gasoline.

The company's motion was made at the end of the Illinois Attorney General's evidence against the refinery, which included video of the fire filmed by a resident near the plant, two state Environmental Protection Agency officials and the local fire chief.

Clark earlier Thursday called one of its customers, Wilfred Kimbel of JLM Chemicals, who testified that his business was being hurt by the partial shutdown of the plant which has cut off his usual supply of propylene and meant he has had to pay more to alternative sources such as Amoco Corp.

The defence argued that the state had not proved anything more than "worry." Clark's attorneys argued that the EPA investigation into last Saturday's fire will take many more weeks and it would be inappropriate to shut the entire plant before it is finished.

The state countered that the plant should be shut until it can be determined why problems continue to occur. The plant has had a series of mishaps in the past two years, including one fire which killed two employees and leaks which caused complaints of lightheadedness by children at a nearby high school.
Clark said it will call at least five more witnesses, which means the hearing is expected to drag into Friday.

Shutting down Clark Refining & Marketing Co's Chicago-area refinery, even temporarily, is expected to rattle Midwest petroleum markets and cause a scramble for gasoline and diesel barrels to cover the lost production, traders said.
Clark operates nearly 830 gasoline stations and convenience stores, selling gasoline and refined products produced at the Blue Island refinery and two other U.S. refineries.
Clark USA Inc, the parent company, is 46 pct owned by The Horsham Corp of Canada and 19 pct by Occidental Petroleum.
